claims.source_quote_ar: من عادته عز وجل في كتابه أن يذكر الترغيب مع الترهيب،
claims.claim_ar: المؤلف يبرز موازنة بلاغية بين الترغيب (البشارة) والترهيب (الإنذار) داخل سياق الأَيَة؛ فذكر ثواب عباد الله الصالحين يقابل ذكر أعمال الكفار وعقابهم.
claims.claim_en: The commentator notes a rhetorical balancing between exhortation (good tidings) and warning (threat); the verse pairs news of reward for the righteous with warning about the disbelievers.
claims.rhetorical_effect: Creates contrast to motivate the believers (hope) while warning the disbelievers (fear), intensifying moral persuasion.

claims.source_quote_ar: وفيه التفات من الغيبة إلى الخطاب.
claims.claim_ar: المصدر يصف ظاهرة بلاغية وهي الالتفات من الحديث عن الغائب إلى مخاطبة السامع/المخاطَب، مما يجذب الانتباه ويقوّي أثر المقطع الختامي للأَيَة.
claims.claim_en: The source describes the rhetorical device of iltifat — a shift from speaking about the absent/third person to addressing the addressee — which draws attention and strengthens the impact of the verse's concluding clause.
claims.needs_review_reason: The quoted discussion is a general note about iltifat in the commentary (on a different example); its direct application to S2:251 is inferred rather than explicitly stated in the provided chunks.
claims.rhetorical_effect: Shifts the listener's focus and engages them directly, increasing immediacy and persuasive force.

warnings: Provided source chunks are mainly from Zamakhshari (al-Kashshaf) and a grammatical excerpt (Safi); no chunks from al-Jurjani, al-Sakkaki, al-Baqillani, al-Suyuti, or an explicit 'tafsir balagha' section were supplied. Claims therefore reflect only the provided material.

Some quoted commentary discusses rhetorical devices in general or with examples from other verses; linking those general remarks to S2:251 is interpretive and noted in the 'needs_review_reason' where appropriate.
